children: Algeria's foreign exchange reserves are set to fall sharply over the next six years, declining from $51 billion in 2025 to $19.8 billion by 2031, the International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday, while noting that higher hydrocarbon revenues could provide an opportunity to rebuild buffers.
The IMF forecasts reserves will fall to $46.5 billion in 2026, $41 billion in 2027, $33.4 billion in 2028, $27.8 billion in 2029, $23.5 billion in 2030 and $19.8 billion in 2031.
It said a wider current account deficit in 2025, driven by higher imports and lower hydrocarbon exports, had contributed to the decline in Algeria's foreign exchange reserves.
The IMF projects GDP growth of 3.8% in 2026 after 3.9% in 2025, with growth slowing to 3.1% in 2027, 3.0% in 2028 and 2029, and 2.9% in 2030 and 2031.

It said Algeria could use higher hydrocarbon revenues to rebuild fiscal and external buffers, but recommended gradual fiscal consolidation, reduced reliance on central bank financing, stronger price stability and greater exchange-rate flexibility.
It also called for continued reforms to diversify the economy and support stronger private-sector-led growth.
